To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the relational algebra is the appropriate tool for investigating programs in terms of partial graphs and that the relational notions of semantics and correctness are equivalent to the corresponding program-theoretic notions.

(1) the flow of control is described by a relation between partial graphs; (2) the single steps are described by a relation on partial graphs; (3) the semantics is obtained by the composition of these two relations; (4) the correctness of a single step is described by a composition of the two relations; and (5) the termination is described by the composition of the two inverse relations
the following two statements hold: (i) A program can be viewed as a partial graph. (ii) A program can always be viewed as a total graph, but the total graph is not necessarily a partial graph.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of program semantics, correctness and termination in terms of partial graphs.
the following questions: (a) How can the flow of control in a program be described in the relational framework?
the investigation of program semantics and correctness by the use of a unified formalism.
